help.title: Help
help.body:
Looking

Sensor: hold the phone up and the stars in that direction appear. Manual: drag with your finger or mouse. Pinch or use the wheel to zoom. On a computer, use the arrow keys and + / −; double-click to center a place.

Tap a star or planet to see its name, brightness, distance and rise/set times.

Search

Use the magnifier at the top right. Follow the arrow and the text (for example “10° right, 5° up”). When the object is in the center, the circle turns green.

Time

“Time” moves the date and time, and can fast forward. Press “Back to now” to return.

Night mode

Red display keeps your eyes used to the dark. “Dim the screen” also helps.

If directions are wrong

The phone compass points to magnetic north. Set the magnetic declination for your area in the menu, and use the fine adjustment. Metal and magnets disturb the compass. Moving the phone in a figure 8 helps.

Star Q&A

How far away is Deneb?
Deneb, the tail of Cygnus, is so far that its distance is hard to measure. Estimates range from about 1,400 to 2,600 light years. It is still easy to see because it shines tens of thousands of times brighter than the Sun.

Why does Albireo look gold and blue?
Albireo, the beak of the Swan, splits into a gold star and a blue star in a small telescope, and is often called the most beautiful double star. The gold one is a cooler orange giant and the blue one is a hot star. To the naked eye it looks like a single star. It is about 430 light years away.

Was Deneb once the pole star?
Earth's axis slowly wobbles like a spinning top, once every 26,000 years (precession), so the pole star changes over time. Today it is Polaris; about 5,000 years ago it was Thuban; about 12,000 to 14,000 years ago the pole was near Vega. The pole passed near Deneb more than ten thousand years ago, when the Swan stood at the center of the night sky. It will pass near Deneb again around the year 10,000.

Does a 'dark matter wind' blow from Cygnus?
The Solar System moves through the Milky Way toward Cygnus at about 230 km/s. Relative to the dark matter thought to fill the galaxy, this means a head wind blows toward Earth from the direction of Cygnus. Experiments around the world are trying to detect the direction of this 'dark matter wind' (it has not been detected yet).

How do I find the Summer Triangle?
On summer and autumn evenings, three bright stars make a large triangle high in the sky: Vega in Lyra, Altair in Aquila, and Deneb in Cygnus. Vega is the brightest, Altair is across the Milky Way, and Deneb sits inside the Milky Way.

Safety

Never look at the Sun, and never look at it with binoculars or a telescope. It can damage your eyes. Be careful in the dark and near water.

Privacy

No ads, no analytics, no tracking. The app makes no requests to other servers; it only loads its own files. Your location is used only on this device to calculate the sky, and it is rounded to about 1 km when saved. Settings are stored only in this browser.

About Starfind

Starfind (working name) is a sky guide that runs in the browser.

Data

Stars: Yale Bright Star Catalogue, 5th ed. (about 9,100 stars to magnitude 6.5). Star names: IAU Catalog of Star Names (WGSN). Constellation lines, borders, Milky Way outline, Messier objects and constellation names in several languages: d3-celestial (Olaf Frohn, BSD-3-Clause). Planets: JPL approximate orbital elements. Japanese names, texts and the meteor shower table were written for this app. Position accuracy is about 0.1–0.5°.

note.polaris: Almost exactly north. Its height above the horizon is about the same as your latitude.
note.vega: The weaving princess star of the Tanabata story. One of the Summer Triangle stars.
note.altair: The cowherd star of the Tanabata story. One of the Summer Triangle stars.
note.deneb: The tail of the Swan. One of the Summer Triangle stars.
note.sun: Do not look at the Sun.
note.shower: Meteors fly out in all directions from the radiant. Watch the whole sky, not only the radiant.
note.cyg: A swan flying along the summer and autumn Milky Way. Deneb is its tail, and the double star Albireo is its beak.
